subject: Request: temporary throughput waiver for Aurora Health pilot
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@aurorahealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Lowe <ben.lowe@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot launch - request for temporary throughput waiver

Hi Rafael,

We kick off our pilot next week and have a short window where traffic will exceed the Hosted baseline rates you quoted. During peak clinic hours we expect short spikes up to ~1,800 req/min for 10-15 minutes and a sustained uplift to ~650 req/min for the first 48 hours as we onboard patient data and run validation.

Our procurement team asked if Redwood can provide a temporary throughput waiver (burst + short-term quota increase) tied to the pilot dates so we don't see throttling that would interrupt the clinician workflow. We also need confirmation that latency SLOs (p95 < 250ms) will be honored during the waiver period or an explicit fallback plan.

Attached: aurora-sla-exception-form.pdf (filled), traffic-heatmap.png

Can we get a short call today to lock this down? Ben from our ops team is on copy.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Director, Digital Programs
Aurora Health Systems

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot launch - request for temporary throughput waiver

Elena —

Thanks for the details and the form. Quick ack: we can support a temporary quota increase but need to align on exact guardrails (burst window length, required latency SLOs, and whether Dedicated capacity is acceptable).

Questions to confirm before we escalate to SRE for allocation:
- Exact pilot window (start/end timestamps, timezone).
- Expected peak bursts (you mentioned 1,800 req/min; any multi-region distribution?).
- Tolerance for throttling: do you want absolute zero throttling, or graceful 429s with retry guidance?
- Which endpoints are in scope (chat generation only, embeddings, or both)?

I copied Laura (account lead) and Stephanie (Enterprise SE) so we can agree on the commercial terms and the operational rollout. If you can confirm the three bullets above I’ll open a formal waiver ticket and share a draft waiver with pricing impact.

I’m available 10:30 PT for a 20-min sync; otherwise we can do asynchronous.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@aurorahealth.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot launch - request for temporary throughput waiver

Elena — great context. 

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) Temporary waiver window: 2027-04-08 00:00 UTC through 2027-04-10 23:59 UTC (72 hours)
2) Scope: chat generation endpoints + low-cost semantic embeddings used for lookup (we will exclude heavy reranking pipelines unless you confirm)
3) Guardrails: burst cap per minute at 2,000 req/min, sustained cap at 700 req/min. We will apply continuous prefix caching for repeated prompts to reduce token count.
4) Latency: we will target p95 < 250ms for text generation on our Hosted fleet but will include an automatic fallback to a compatible, lower-cost model if latency exceeds 350ms for >2 consecutive 5-min windows. We will notify you and route to Dedicated if required.
5) Pricing: temporary uplift billed at 1.6x standard hosted rate for tokens during the waiver window (see attached pricing-impact.xlsx). We can convert to a short-term committed burst for a lower uplift if you prefer.

Next steps: Rafael will open an internal waiver ticket and route to SRE for capacity checks. Elena — if the window and scope above look good please reply with explicit approval and include your procurement contact for DocuSign.

Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
Attached: pricing-impact.xlsx
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@aurorahealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Lowe <ben.lowe@aurorahealth.com>, procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot launch - request for temporary throughput waiver

Thanks Laura — the MAP looks reasonable and we're happy to accept the proposed window and scope. Two quick clarifications:
- We confirm chat generation + embeddings only (no reranking).
- Procurement copied on this thread for DocuSign: procurement@aurorahealth.com (please send the waiver + short amendment).

Approval: Aurora Health Systems approves the temporary waiver as outlined. Please proceed.

Elena

Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: opening SLA waiver ticket for Aurora (action: SRE allocation + runbook)

Stephanie / Laura —

Per Aurora's approval I submitted WAIVER-2842 to SRE with the following asks:
- Provision temporary burst headroom on Hosted fleet: +2x traffic for 72h window (2027-04-08T00:00Z - 2027-04-10T23:59Z).
- Apply prefix/KV caching and token-aware batching for the pilot routes.
- Canary plan: incrementally ramp at 20% every 10 minutes and monitor p95; auto-fallback to smaller model if p95 > 350ms for two consecutive 5-minute checks.
- Notify Aurora procurement when DocuSign is sent; I attached the draft waiver to the ticket (link below).

Link: https://internal.redwood.com/sre/tickets/WAIVER-2842
Related HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-2024-0543

I’ll update the thread when SRE confirms capacity. Rafael
